The **PULP trial** (Peptic Ulcer Perforation trial) is a multi-center intervention study led by [[moller-mh|Møller MH]] that investigated the effects of multimodal perioperative care for patients with perforated peptic ulcers [^src1]. The trial serves as a foundational piece of registry research, providing the scientific and methodological background for the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (Acute Surgery Database) [^src1]. 

The findings from the PULP trial directly inform clinical practice and national quality monitoring in Denmark. Its multimodal perioperative care protocol and prognostic scales, such as the PULP score, form the evidence base for multiple quality indicators within the database, specifically those concerning preoperative optimization and risk assessment [^src1]. Furthermore, the study—which was conducted in the late 2000s (noted as "slut nullerne" in the 2024 report, albeit with a typographical error as "PUPL")—demonstrated the critical importance of rapid medical intervention for this vulnerable patient population [^src2]. This evidence supports the policy and prioritization behind time-based surgical metrics like [[indikator-4x|Indikator 4x]], which monitors life-threatening emergency conditions including perforations [^src2]. By grounding its indicators in trials like PULP, the Acute Surgery Database ensures its 11 clinical quality metrics are rigorously evidence-based and tied to specific treatment goals and deadlines [^src1].
